You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

=== autocomplete-suggestion-count ===
title: Allow plugins to customize number of suggestions in autocomplete
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Some plugins need far more or far fewer autocomplete suggestions than Jenkins’s hard-coded default, but today they cannot express that preference in the rendered control.


  ## Desired outcome


  Plugin authors should be able to set the maximum suggestion count per autocomplete field without forking the widget.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget still defaults to 10 suggestions when nothing is specified, but a field can override that limit through the `data-maxsuggestions` attribute.

  '
=== updatesite-subclass-updatedata ===
title: Allow subclasses of UpdateSite to call updateData
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin developers who subclass `UpdateSite` may need to reuse Jenkins’ built-in metadata parsing and validation path, but the core implementation hides `updateData(String json, boolean signatureCheck)` from subclasses and forces unnecessary duplication.


  ## Desired outcome

  `UpdateSite` subclasses should be able to invoke `updateData(String json, boolean signatureCheck)` directly as part of their own update processing while preserving the same validation behavior core uses. This is a developer-facing API improvement, not a change in how standard update sites behave for administrators.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A subclass of `UpdateSite` can call `updateData(String json, boolean signatureCheck)` without reflection or copy-pasted logic, the shared parsing and signature-check flow remains intact, and standard Jenkins update-site behavior stays the same.

  '
=== boot-version-logging ===
title: Print Jenkins version on boot
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator starting or upgrading a controller often needs to confirm from the startup logs exactly which Jenkins version is coming up, but boot logs do not currently state that version explicitly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When Jenkins starts, the normal startup log should include the controller version so administrators can confirm the running build without inferring it from package metadata or the UI. The boot message should clearly report the value returned by `Jenkins.getVersion()`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Startup logs include a message containing the current Jenkins version during initialization, operators can confirm the running version from boot output alone, and no extra manual step is required to verify which release started.

  '
=== plugin-download-source-url ===
title: Show plugin source URL when downloading it
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  When Jenkins downloads a plugin during installation or upgrade, operators can see the plugin name in logs but not the exact source URL, which makes mirror issues and provenance checks harder.


  ## Desired outcome


  Download logging should show the concrete plugin URL Jenkins is fetching so administrators can diagnose slow or unexpected sources without extra debugging.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The download message names the plugin and includes the full source URL that Jenkins is using for that artifact.

  '
=== user-reload-beta-api ===
title: Expose `User.reload` as beta API
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin developers and advanced integrators need to know which `User` APIs are still experimental before they depend on them, but `User.reload()` currently looks like an ordinary stable entry point even though it is not meant to be treated that way yet.


  ## Desired outcome

  `User.reload()` should be explicitly marked as Beta API so consumers understand that the method is available but not yet part of Jenkins’ stable long-term contract. This is a contract-clarity change rather than a behavioral one.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The public API documentation for `User.reload()` clearly indicates beta status, plugin authors can distinguish it from stable user APIs, and existing runtime behavior of the reload operation is unchanged.

  '
=== inbound-agent-websocket-default ===
title: Add -webSocket option by default when creating an inbound agent

requirement: '## Context

category: ci

  ## Desired outcome


  Keep the discarder behavior the same while removing routine chatter from its listener output.
